text:
elaine: quick follow-up from the canary/a-b rollout sync — i sketched a short proposal to split decision tenancy from enforcement. central controller makes rollout decisions and issues short-lived tokens; local agents enforce and have a small emergency escape hatch when infra pressure or safety signals spike. want quick reactions on tradeoffs and the telemetry contract we need.
sam: +1 for split tenancy. can we be explicit about which signals are authoritative vs advisory? e.g., p99 latency and error-rate authoritative for SLA, but cpu/queue-length advisory for local fast-fail.
raj: curious about push vs pull model between controller and agent. push = lower latency for new rollouts, pull = resilient to controller outage. hybrid?
marta: hybrid seems sensible: controller pushes decisions; agents keep last-known decision with TTL and poll fallback channel. if TTL expires, agent auto-deg-steps (route back to stable variant) instead of blocking requests.
kevin: two immediate concerns: 1) split-brain if controller restarts and reissues new decisions with overlapping ids; 2) churn on high-frequency canaries causing noise. suggest decision epochs + idempotent tokens. tokens include epoch, decision_id, signature.
elaine: agree on epoch + token. propose fields: {
  "decision_id": "uuid",
  "epoch": "64-bit monotonic",
  "routes": [ {"variant": "v2", "pct": 0.02} ],
  "ttl_ms": 300000,
  "sig": "hex"
} as a minimal control message.
raj: looks good. edgecase: what if agent applies partial update (applies route but fails to set cache warmup)? need an apply-transaction concept or idempotent steps.
sam: agent should publish apply-status back to controller with simple states: PENDING -> APPLIED -> READY -> FAILED. controller can retry or escalate. lightweight protocol over existing telemetry channel works.
marta: telemetry contract: controller expects per-variant timeseries: p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate (5xx + model-eval-fail), queue-length, kv-cache-hit-rate, and synthetic probe success/failure. buckets by route+model+tenant. also need sampling rate guidance to avoid cost explosion.
kevin: emphasize dimension cardinality limits. we must cap tenant dims and do sampling + rollup. controller only needs roll-level aggregates for decisioning (not per-request traces). for debugging we sample more.
elaine: on privacy: per-tenant telemetry must be optionally redacted for private deployments. controllers in private mode should accept pseudonymized keys or local-only reporting.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary v2 -> eu-west-1 started for service inference-router (canary id 0a1b). :rocket:
raj: good reminder — need an admission contract: agents validate token sig, verify epoch monotonicity, then schedule rollout. validation steps must be cheap and avoid crypto thrash: HMAC with shared key + optional rotation.
sam: fallback semantics: we need two flavors — soft fallback (shift pct back to stable over N seconds) and hard fallback (immediate 100% revert) for safety. agents must support both. controller chooses based on signal severity and policy.
marta: sample policy DSL example: 
````
policy: {
  trigger: { error_rate: { window_s: 60, threshold: 0.05 } },
  action: { type: "soft_revert", duration_s: 300, step_pct: 0.2 }
}
````
(three backticks inside thread kept as fenced code)
kevin: edge: cascading fallbacks across regional agents — when eu-west reverts, traffic might spike in us-east. controller should simulate capacity shift and can pre-declare cross-region drain budgets. local agents need backpressure signals to upstream load balancers.
elaine: good point. add cross-region capacity delta estimate to decision metadata. agents publish capacity headroom metric. controller will include a predicted global shift plan when making multi-region changes.
sam: operational simplicity: keep controller thin — only makes decisions, emits tokens, collects aggregation. heavy logic (probe retries, warmup) stays local. this reduces controller latency and failure blast radius.
raj: agree. also: require a small test harness for offline simulation (replay p99 lat traces + decision logic) before any rollout. can we make the TLS+API backward-compatible with current rollout infra?
marta: yes, design controller API to accept v1 tokens and v2 tokens. agents check version field and fallback accordingly.
kevin: next steps: elaine to draft RFC with state machine diagrams, sample control message schema, token lifecycle, and telemetry contract. sam to add api wire format and sampling guidance. marta to prototype agent-side apply-state machine. raj to drive simulation harness. i'll coordinate cross-region capacity hooks.
elaine: thanks — i'll ping owners and create the RFC PR tomorrow. please add any quick objections here. otherwise i'll label this as RFC-next-step and schedule a 30m follow-up. :thumbsup:
